title: Under Armour Cuts Sales View on Softer Demand Around the World
summary:
Under Armour Inc. forecast a sharper revenue decline than previously expected as demand softens in several key regions.
The athletic retailer now expects sales to fall by a mid-single digit percentage rate for the year. The revised forecast calls for declines in North America, Asia-Pacific, and Europe and the Middle East as the company grapples with a “challenging consumer demand environment,” Chief Executive Officer Kevin Plank said in a statement Friday. Bloomberg's Poonam Goyal joined Bloomberg Intelligence to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Congo to Investigate Reports of Excess Uranium in Cobalt Exports
summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo will look into reports of excess uranium leaving the country in its exports of battery mineral cobalt, the government said Thursday.

title: Stocks and Bonds Rise as Jobs Ease Fed-Hike Wagers: Markets Wrap
summary: A sharp slowdown in the US jobs market drove stocks higher while bond yields fell on speculation the Federal Reserve won’t be forced to raise interest rates any time soon.

title: BlackRock’s Rieder Sees AI Helping Buoy GDP Even as Hiring Slows
summary: BlackRock Inc.’s Rick Rieder said last month’s surprise contraction in payrolls reflects a “productivity revolution” rather than economic weakness, arguing that the US economy remains on track for 6% nominal growth in gross domestic product even as hiring stalls.

title: Fitch Sees Chile Budget as Key to Halting Rising Debt Burden
summary: Fitch Ratings is skeptical that tax cuts approved by Chile’s Congress last month will boost growth by enough to offset the immediate drop in revenue, leaving the emphasis on fiscal spending reductions if the government wants to balance the books anytime soon.

title: Treasuries Rally as Soft Jobs Data Trims Fed Rate-Hike Bets
summary: US Treasuries rallied after data showed employers unexpectedly cut jobs in July, suggesting labor market challenges that could impact the Federal Reserve’s willingness to raise interest rates.

title: US Stocks Jump as Jobs Data Seen Easing Rate Hike Pressures
summary: US stocks rose on Friday after jobs data showed the US economy unexpectedly shed jobs in July, which could prompt the Federal Reserve to delay interest-rate increases.

title: Once-AAA Bonds on New York Megamall Face Over $350 Million Loss
summary: Pyramid Management Group, a shopping center developer, is buying back the mortgage on a struggling megamall it owns in Syracuse, New York, for cents on the dollar, mostly wiping out bonds that originally carried top ratings.

title: 4% Rule Doesn't Reflect Realities of Retirement, Says Bruce Wolfe
summary:
Soaring markets have swollen the ranks of 401(k) millionaires, and companies have largely freed themselves from costly traditional pension plans in favor of self-directed, employee-funded savings that bestow tax benefits on employers and workers.
Bruce Wolfe, founder at CS Wolfe & Associates, discusses how inflation and market uncertainty are changing the way we save for, and spend during, retirement. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Port of LA Partners with California for Vincent Thomas Bridge Project
summary:
US importers are rushing goods into the nation’s two busiest ports, pushing up ocean transport costs during the wait for more tariffs and an extended bout of economic uncertainty stemming from the Iran war.
Gene Seroka, CEO of the Port of Los Angeles, discusses port labor, innovation, and supply shocks impacting trade with the US. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 7
summary: Oil gained as tensions in the Middle East flared while traders monitored progress toward a deal between Iran and Oman to partially restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: US Employers Cut Jobs, Unemployment Rate Falls
summary:
Nonfarm payrolls decreased 23,000 last month following a combined 103,000 downward revision to the May and June figures, Bureau of Labor Statistics data showed Friday. 
The unemployment rate fell to 4.1% as labor force participation continued to slide, and wage growth slowed.
Claudia Sahm, Chief Economist at New Century Advisors and Constance Hunter, Chief Economist at EIU, react to July jobs data. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Yen Jumps on US Data as Traders Watch for Intervention Clues
summary: The yen surged against a weaker dollar after an unexpectedly soft US payrolls report on Friday, offering the latest fodder for speculation that authorities could intervene in the Japanese currency again.

title: How a Sardine Gets From the Ocean to a Can

The category took off during Covid and now shoppers are shelling out for high end brands like Fishwife. Today’s guest Becca Millstein started the company in 2020, positioning it as a distinct, artisanal product, more akin to one might find in European grocery stores.
